proposal.reason_no_apply: T4 is purely additive — it emits bilateral_gap as telemetry alongside depth, but does NOT change the decision logic. Per task spec 'решение-логика НЕ меняется'. Tuning depthFloor or adding a bilateralFloor threshold would belong to a future T5 (which would also need a larger labeled corpus to validate against overfitting to 96 pairs).

phase4_calibration.correction_to_t3_calibration: T3 calibration's heuristic checked `boundary_depth_p25 < same_topic_depth_p25` (WRONG direction for depth — at a boundary cosine DIPS so depth = ema_baseline - cosine RISES). With the correct direction `boundary_p25 > same_topic_p25` the T3 sample also had separable depth: -0.0627 > -0.0751 (delta 0.0124). However, the T3 effect size was small and current depthFloor=0.12 catches only 9/95 candidate decisions. T4 confirms the same separability pattern on a fresh run (96 pairs) with cleaner effect_size = 0.4865.

vs_t3.interpretation: T4 produced identical chunk structure (17 final, same min/median/max) but caught one fewer true boundary (6/7 vs 7/7). The drop is likely streaming nondeterminism: T4 has more deadline-triggered chunks (27 vs 20) and fewer marker-triggered (6 vs 8), suggesting the drift-merge in offline pass made a different decision on one boundary. Same total after offline (17). Precision unchanged at 0.75 — 4 extra chunk boundaries still mis-aligned within ±2 sentences (same drift-merge artifact as T3).

key_findings.1: T4 is purely additive telemetry — decision logic unchanged. F1 0.8 vs T3 0.857 is within streaming nondeterminism; not a regression caused by T4 code.
key_findings.2: ALL THREE signals are separable by p25 (cosine, depth, bilateral_gap). The T3 conclusion that 'depth not separable' was a heuristic direction bug in calibration-t3.mjs — corrected here.
key_findings.3: Best signal by Cohen's d effect size: depth (0.4865) > bilateral_gap (0.4367) > cosine (0.431). Difference between depth and bilateral_gap is small (~0.05) — neither dominates.
key_findings.4: bilateral_gap (TextTiling-style) does NOT dramatically improve separability over depth on bge-m3 with 96 pairs — the EMA was not the bottleneck for this dataset. The non-adaptive hypothesis from t4-impl-report is not supported here; bilateral_gap is on par with depth, not clearly better.
key_findings.5: Current depthFloor=0.12 only catches 9/96 candidate decisions (same as T3 9/95). Most boundary signal sits below this threshold. A future T5 could explore lower depthFloor (~0.05) OR add a bilateralFloor threshold (e.g. median-diff=0.0313 → floor ~0.40) to broaden the trigger — but this requires more labeled data to validate against overfitting to one monolog.

notes: Docker rebuild + retest pipeline ran end-to-end without orphans on a 1ms/packet pace (78.1s stream + ~5s flush + offline). Same flow as T3 v2.
T4 implements purely additive telemetry (bilateral_gap as wire event field) — does not change commit/candidate logic. EMA-depth still drives the boundary detector, as designed.
All 7 true block boundaries from monolog-meta.json were within ±30 words of 42 semantic_debug sentences; same labeling as T3 calibration.
Precision 0.75 floor persists — 4 chunk boundaries that don't match true boundaries within ±2 sentences. Likely drift-merge splitting behavior, same as T3.
open_questions: If depth IS separable (corrected heuristic), why does current depthFloor=0.12 only catch 9/96 candidates? — boundary depth p25=-0.0627 is BELOW 0.12, so most boundary signal never crosses threshold. Future T5: lower depthFloor to ~0.05 (boundary p25) and re-test F1.

Bilateral_gap and depth are nearly equivalent in separability (effect_size diff = 0.05) — is there a meaningful reason to keep both, or pick one? — needs a second monolog to disambiguate, otherwise the choice is overfit to this dataset.
T4 F1 dropped 0.057 vs T3 (6/7 vs 7/7 recall). Is this a real regression or run-to-run noise? — needs 3+ reruns on same image to bound variance.
